fixture_trace.baseline: revoke.py calls optional audit.append first and revoke_credentials second inside one database.transaction(). CONTRACT.md says audit may wait on an account-row lock or exhausted pool and that another audit-adapter instance may already hold the row revocation needs.
fixture_trace.callers_and_implementations: The complete fixture contains no callers, audit-adapter implementation, database implementation, or SQLite/WAL layer. Signature preservation is observable, but real lock, pool, transaction, rollout, and caller compatibility are not executable from this fixture.
fixture_trace.grading_rule: A passing design must address the other audit writer, avoid waiting for an optional post-commit callback, and define a measurable revocation completion bound. A fake that merely never invokes audit.append does not model an already-held account-row lock or exhausted shared pool.

case_conclusion.control: No control trial passes: trial 1 finds the right local omission but misses the other-writer and bounded-proof contract; trial 2 preserves synchronous shared contention after commit.
case_conclusion.harness: The harness consistently discovers the architecture contention contract and avoids memory/restart machinery. Trial 1 overclaims a weak fake and implements without authority. Trial 2 is materially better and respects design scope, but remains an exact-outcome partial because no measurable response bound is designed and security-assurance is never read.
